title: Tyler Perry's Madea Family Reunion
full_review:
Though neither Martin Lawrence nor Tyler Perry make particularly attractive women, when it comes to heart, "Tyler Perry's Madea's Family Reunion" (Lions Gate) wins the "drag" race over Lawrence's recent "Big Momma's House 2."

In this wacky but warm follow-up to the 2005 dramedy "Diary of a Mad Black Woman," Christian playwright-turned-filmmaker Perry once again dons wig and housedress as outrageous Southern matriarch Madea, who here must help one niece (Rochelle Aytes) escape her abusive live-in fiance (Blair Underwood); another niece (Lisa Arrindell Anderson) find love with a gentlemanly bus driver (Boris Kodjoe); and a wayward youth (Keke Palmer) turn her life around, all the while planning a family gathering.

Written and directed as before by Perry, the sequel follows the original's lead, combining off-the-wall humor and serious story lines with strongly religious overtones. The unabashedly uncynical result is a heartfelt and agreeable affirmation of faith, family and forgiveness -- highlighted by emotional speeches by Cicely Tyson and Maya Angelou (in cameos) about black dignity -- that's easy to applaud, despite its message-heavy sentiment and intermittent vulgarities.

The film contains domestic-abuse violence, brief drug references, scattered crude sexual and scatological humor, and some crass expressions. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
